summary: Climber fell from the Great White Wall in Black Canyon of the Gunnison and was knocked unconscious with major traumatic injuries; NPS teams descended 1,800 ft and a Guard helicopter flew the patient out.
location: Great White Wall, North Rim, Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park
responding_agency: National Park Service; Colorado Army National Guard helicopter; medical air ambulance (to St. Mary's Hospital, Grand Junction)
notes: Fall ~10:30am Monday; rescue teams hiked to North Rim, dropped 1,800 ft in, scaled 300 ft to climber, lowered to canyon bottom; helicopter evacuation ~7:30pm. Subject identified via the AAC Accidents narrative: Becca Steinbrecher, 30; her partner Skyeler Congdon, 40, rappelled the route and drove to the North Rim ranger station for help after securing her to an anchor (concerned about a spinal injury). 28-person SAR team (Black Canyon NPS + Western Colorado University SAR), CO Army National Guard HAATS Black Hawk flew her out ~7:25 p.m., transferred to medical air ambulance in Montrose, then to St. Mary's in Grand Junction with major trauma injuries. Run-493 merge: Climbing magazine feature (opened; published 2023-09-19) identifies the fallen climber as Becca, 30, of Grand Junction, with partner Skyeler Congdon; fall ~7:30 a.m. Monday from ~30 ft up the fourth pitch of The Great White Wall (IV 5.10d, 1,300 ft) after a foothold broke and a yellow TCU ripped; multiple broken bones, punctured lung, severe head injury, unconscious ~11 hours; HAATS Black Hawk hoist ~7 p.m.; coma/critical condition at St. Mary's, slow recovery. | blca.htm NPS morning-report entry confirms date/location: Sept-11-2023 technical rope rescue on the Great White Wall route, North Rim (Long Draw approach, ~300-ft climb, lower to canyon floor), Army National Guard helicopter to Montrose then medical air ambulance to St. Mary's, Grand Junction.
